then.text: I'm still putting this sign up. It won't hammer itself.
Please do not roam while I'm working. It makes the paperwork wobble.

else.text: Halt! This stretch of moorland is now the property of the Enclosure.
It's the A537. It's a road.
Was the A537. Lord Vane has bought the view. And the heather. And the fog.
I'm putting up a sign. It says PRIVATE: NO ROAMING in a very firm font.

then.text: I'm roaming. Look. I'm roaming right now.
You can't. The sign isn't even up yet! Wait, that's worse for me.

else.text: The fog is a Heritage Feature, and we don't discuss its terms.
Lord Vane says it adds atmosphere. It adds about nine bruises a week.
Right. Carry on, then. But I'll be noting it down. In triplicate.

cat_scene.text: Something small and black is sat in the road ahead, washing a paw. It stops with one leg in the air and looks at you.
You know that look. You have been given it across the kitchen every morning since you were small.
...Is that you? Mum's been putting your breakfast out for days.
She walks up, sniffs your hand, then {lead}, then your hand again. Her eyes are a green they were not before.
Whatever she saw up on the moor the night the stones hummed, she has come back a little more than a cat.
{lead} and the cat look at each other for a long moment. Something is settled without you.
Mum is going to be unbearable about this.
There is only one of her, and she is yours. If she ever wants a lie-down, Mum will keep her by the bowl at home.
